title: store unfinished mark
description: The mark of a change the store is making, a file .unfinished-<id>.json that mankit's store writes in the .queue/ folder of every turn the change holds: the served folder's own and each thing's (ADR-S14). A dot-file, so the change queue's rules leave it alone, and it outlives a ticket taken for stale (README, The change queue on disk). While a mark is there, every change to a key it names is refused with unfinished_change, naming the user, the machine and the app's command that clears the mark, until that user's next run puts the journal back and removes the mark; only the user who owns a journal puts it back (ADR-S22). Its lifetime is the journal's: written before the journal, removed after it, last, before the turn is given up (StoreJournal). When that user never runs again, a person may clear the mark through the app's own command (such as <app> store unfinished clear <thing>), which shows the change and asks first (G-STACK-13), once sure the change was put back or given up; nothing clears a mark unasked. Two app versions may read one mark: apiVersion, kind and metadata never change; spec may grow (ADR-S15).

apiVersion.description: The form of the store's files, the same as a journal's. It never changes, so two app versions both read every mark (ADR-S15).

kind.description: Always StoreUnfinished. It tells a mark apart from a journal's lines, which carry the same apiVersion.

metadata.description: Which mark it is. It never changes in v1, since every app version reads every mark by it (ADR-S15).

id.description: The mark's name and its file name between .unfinished- and .json, the same in every .queue/ folder the change writes it to, so the marks of one change are found together (a StoreJournal's spec.mark names it). 20 digits made like a ticket id, from the time and a random part, so it is one of a kind among the marks of every folder it is written to, whichever user wrote them.

user.description: The user whose data folder holds the journal, by the name the system knows them by, so the refusal names who must run again.

host.description: The machine the journal is on, as it names itself, since a user keeps one journal per machine (ADR-S22), so the refusal says where to run again.

journal.description: The id of the journal that holds the change (a StoreJournal's metadata.id), so that user's next run finds the change to put back.

folder.description: true when the change also holds the served folder's own turn, as adding, moving or removing a thing does (ADR-S14), so a change to the folder itself is refused too. Left out when false.

keys.description: Every key the change writes, a new thing's too, whose turn is the served folder's (ADR-S14), so each copy of the mark names the whole change, whichever queue a later change meets it in, and a change to a key it names, or to one inside a folder key it names, is refused.

spec.description: What the mark says about the change. Open: a newer app may add fields here, and an older reader accepts them (CT-RULE-4). A field a newer app adds never changes what the mark holds back; a mark an older reader could not obey is a new kind or a new version.
